PIMA.name: PIMA Indians Diabetes Dataset
PIMA.target_definition: Existing status: 2-hour post-load plasma glucose >= 200 mg/dl
PIMA.population: Adult females of Pima Indian heritage (Arizona, USA)
PIMA.transferability_constraint: Features (Insulin, OGTT glucose) are invasive laboratory measurements. Cannot be calculated from survey data.

CDC_BRFSS.name: CDC Diabetes Health Indicators
CDC_BRFSS.target_definition: Self-reported doctor diagnosis of diabetes (Survey question)
CDC_BRFSS.population: Broad civilian, non-institutionalized US adult population
CDC_BRFSS.transferability_constraint: Contains subjective self-reports and categorized ordinal bins. Zero biological lab measurements.

UCI_SYMPTOM.name: UCI Early Stage Diabetes Risk Prediction
UCI_SYMPTOM.transferability_constraint: Symptoms (Polyuria, Polydipsia) are immediate physiological consequences of hyperglycemia. Not predictive of pre-diabetes.

shared_features: Age (continuous in PIMA, binned in CDC)
PIMA_vs_CDC.reason: Missing invasive biochemical markers in CDC survey.

PIMA_vs_UCI.reason: PIMA records clinical metrics; UCI records symptomatic complaints.

CDC_vs_UCI.reason: CDC surveys long-term lifestyle habits; UCI surveys acute physiological symptoms.

scientific_and_engineering_decision: FORCING HARMONIZATION IS SCIENTIFICALLY FLAWED: Attempting to merge or impute missing features across these three datasets to force an artificial unified feature space would introduce massive synthetic variance and violate clinical validity. Therefore, DiabetesGuard AI explicitly maintains THREE DEDICATED SPECIALIZED TRACKS: (1) Clinical Assessment Module, (2) Non-Invasive Lifestyle Screener, and (3) Acute Symptom Checker. Each module runs its own validated, calibrated model suited to its context.
